nodes.text: explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Locate the Fireship channel and retrieve its full video list; filter to videos published between 2024-01-01 and 2025-12-31 inclusive, sort by view count descending, and select the top 10 (or all available if fewer than 10). For each selected video collect `video_id`, `title`, `published_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `duration_seconds`, `view_count`, `like_count`, and a concise `primary_topic` technology label derived from the video tags or, if tags are unavailable, the title keywords. Return the compact ten-row table plus channel/page/date/count controls. Do not write files or create deliverables.

coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of `Tech_Trend_Report.xlsx`. Read only the frozen packet. Create a `Videos` sheet holding exactly 10 data rows (one per video, in the given order) with columns `Video_ID, Title, Published_Date, Duration_Seconds, View_Count, Like_Count, Primary_Topic` in that order, and a `Topic_Summary` sheet with one row per distinct `Primary_Topic` giving `Video_Count`, `Total_Views`, and `Avg_Duration` (rounded to at most 2 decimals) computed from the frozen Videos data. If the video data is incomplete, build the workbook with the valid rows. Write literal values and read every populated range back.

coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of a page titled exactly `Fireship Tech Trends Q1 2026`. Search the exact title first, create at most once on zero matches, and block on duplicates. Include an `Overview` heading with a summary paragraph covering the 10 videos analyzed in 2024-2025, the most frequent topic(s) by video count, and the top topic by total views. Add a `Top 5 Technology Topics by Total Views` section with a table of Topic, Video_Count, and Total_Views for the top 5 topics sorted by Total_Views descending. Read the page back.

coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole calendar owner. Search existing `Tech Review` events in March 2026, then create a weekly recurring event titled `Tech Review Meeting` starting Monday 2026-03-09 from 14:00 to 15:00 UTC, repeating every Monday at that time. If an identical event (same title, start time, and weekly recurrence) already exists, treat it as the deliverable instead of creating a duplicate. Read the retained event back.
